# Core Flight System - **Demo** Bundle

The Core Flight System (cFS) is a generic flight software architecture framework used on flagship spacecraft, human spacecraft, cubesats, and Raspberry Pi. This repository is a bundle containing submodules that make up the cFS framework. **Note the "lab" apps are demos intended as examples only, and enable this bundle to build, execute, receive commands, and send telemetry. This is not a flight distribution, which is typically made up of the cFE, OSAL, PSP, and a selection of flight apps that correspond to specific mission requirements. It should not be flown as is.**

**This bundle has not been fully verified** as an operational system, and is provided as a starting point as opposed an end product. Testing of this bundle consists of building, executing, sending setup commands and verifying receipt of telemetry. Unit testing is also run, but extensive analysis is not performed. All verification and validation per mission requirements is the responsibility of the mission (although attempts are made in the cFS Framework to provide a testing framework to facilitate the process).

The cFS Framework is a core subset of cFS, with an extensive ecosystem of applications and tools available throughout the community.

## cFS Versioning and Updates

cFS follows a [semantic](https://semver.org/) versioning convention. Release candidates are denoted with the "rc[#]" suffix. Bug/vulnerability fixes are addressed in the next sequential release of cFS. For cFS open source, these fixes are **not** backported to prior releases. Users are encouraged to upgrade to the latest version of cFS. For users who are not able to upgrade, see [cFS Gov](#cfs-gov-mission-ready-version)

## Distributions

This is the open-source version of cFS, released under an Apache 2.0 license. The open source cFS is limited to the framework and common apps, libraries, and tools, which includes and is limited to: cFE, OSAL, PSP, Command Ingest Lab (Demo), Telemetry Output Lab (Demo), Scheduler Lab (Demo), Sample App (Demo), Sample Lib (Demo), Data Storage, File Manager, HouseKeeping, Health and Safety, Memory Dwell, CFDP File Transfer, CheckSum, Limit Checker, Stored Command, cFS Ground System, elf2cfetbl, and tblCRCTool. Changes to the open repositories are limited to bug fixes and minor enhancements to those components.

### cFS Gov (Mission-Ready Version)

A Government-use (Distro C) version of cFS with features, certifiability, and security measures for a full flight mission is available through a Software User Agreement. For more information about government version features or to explore partnerships, please [contact the cFS team](<mailto:cfs-program@lists.nasa.gov>).

## Contact

cFS/cFE is owned and maintained by NASA's [Core cFS Team](https://etd.gsfc.nasa.gov/capabilities/core-flight-system/core-team/) and [Steering Committee](https://etd.gsfc.nasa.gov/capabilities/core-flight-system/steering-committee/).

The cFS team provides training, support, and subject matter expertise to cFS users across industry and the government. New features/developments can also be developed by the cFS team, which has significant experience in helping flight projects implement mission-ready flight software using cFS for various classes of missions, including human-rated (class A) missions. A support agreement may be needed.

To connect with the cFS team, please send an email to [cfs-program@lists.nasa.gov](<mailto:cfs-program@lists.nasa.gov>).

More information is available on the [cFS Website](<https://cfs.gsfc.nasa.gov>).
